analyst_view.overall: Early view: City lost three league games in a row before the break, with Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol coming off with knocks at Forest, and they play Leeds three days earlier. Brentford are eighth but lost at Brighton, where Igor Thiago was sent off; a standard three-game ban for violent conduct would end before this match, so he may be back, though I did not find the ban length confirmed. City conceding in transition is Brentford's opening.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly higher: Maresca admitted City conceded twice in transition at Forest after losing duels in midfield, and Brentford are built for quick attacks. If Thiago is back from his ban, Brentford have their main target man too.

corners.text: The site has 10.2 corners. I agree: City will have the ball and earn corners, and Brentford's quick breaks should win a few of their own. Nothing points strongly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean higher: Brentford have had two players sent off this season, and City's recent problems with intensity mean they could foul more to stop counters. A night game under the lights with both sides needing points adds to that.

shots.text: The site has 26.5 shots. I agree: City will take a lot of shots, and Brentford get their chances in transition. The only doubt is City rotating with a Champions League game the following week.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I agree: Haaland and Cherki usually test the goalkeeper, and Brentford's counters lead to clear chances. Caoimhin Kelleher should be busy.
